newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest bourse extends gains in heavy demand.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest bourse extends gains in heavy demand.

text.p: Average as well as closing quotes of most Bucharest stocks jogged higher on Friday as the market ended a week of active buying, mostly by foreigners.
"Recent foreign investment rules proved an incentive and foreign demand was strong," a trader said. "There was local interest, too, also from retailers due to lower deposit rates."
A stock exchange Friday report showed average price gainers led decliners 27 to five, with two stocks staying flat. Nine companies had no deal and two were suspended.

Three independent market indices, the VAB, the BIG and the CAS-SE, based on average prices and market capitalisation, touched new year highs, rising by 3.5, 3.65 and 3.46 percent respectively from Thursday.
Short-term rates on banking deposits recently dropped to an average 60 percent from 110 percent.
Brokers saw the market moving ahead next week. "There's lots of money in the market, demand will stay heavy," said one.
Friday's volume was 3.5 million shares, some 500,000 up from the previous session, while turnover gained 3.3 billion lei to 15.8 billion.

There were also two special trades -- deals outside the bourse, reported later -- worth a total 1.3 billion lei, in more than 300,000 shares in fertiliser maker Azomures. Traders said there was foreign interest behind those deals.
Romania issued investor-friendly legislation, including portfolio rules, which set a tax per deal of up to 1.5 percent.
The first tier was most active with 93 percent of turnover. Four of the eight stocks in this section closed higher, two retreated and one marked time. Arctic refrigerator maker remained suspended.

Antibiotice and Terapia pharmaceuticals gained 50 and 150 lei respectively to 7,600 and 7,850. Oltchim chemical plant ended 300 lei stronger at 3,900 and Policolor dye maker, which moved to the first tier on Friday, firmed 200 lei to 6,750.
Compa vehicle parts maker lost 100 lei to 3,100 and fertiliser maker Sofert closed 500 lei weaker at 32,000. Azomures stayed flat at 3,950 lei.
